title: Remove no longer used enterprises.tsv file

notes.body: /cc @geraldcombs Requires changes to update-ws-numbers, specifically `tools/make-sminmpec.py` should be invoked from the top source dir without any arguments.
That shouldn't be a problem. Would it make sense to rename the script to  "make-enterprises.py" or something similar?
I think it would make a lot of sense. I also would like to rename the C file (to something a bit shorter). Will update the MR.
Done.
Just a reminder, update-ws-numbers also needs `COMMIT_FILES+=("enterprises.c")`.

The weekly update script has been updated.
mentioned in commit geraldcombs/update-ws-numbers@ae2d6fa85937c3d799076c0fe51e05d8c6ce587c
This is a generated file.
The intended usage of the "generated files" build variable is for build subproducts (lemon and flex files mainly).

I was only vaguely aware that the enterprises file existed before noticing how long it took to load in a performance profile.  The plan (hopefully sometime in the next couple of weeks) is to do a similar change with manuf for ethernet vendor codes.

My thought was to leave the global files as part of the installation, to make overriding them more discoverable (and to give examples of the formats that would be used), and that it makes sense to write into comments at the top of both files explaining that these global files will not be (re-)read, but if someone wants to override/add entries, they should copy the filename and format but in their personal or profile folder.
Adding a skeleton file to the personal folder seems reasonable. Keeping an unused large file in the global folder seem wasteful and not particularly useful to users.
If it is OK with you I would like to help. I will start converting the services file.
Yes, please do.  It'll be a few days before I'm able to spend more than a few minutes at a time on this.

I don't know if you ran another profile, but in the last one I did parsing (and reparsing) services took 2.47% of the run.  However, it also spent 36% time parsing protobuf files, so you could probably scale all of these figures up somewhat.

Oops - added my $.02 to the other MR:  
https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/11358#note_1462677227
